findings.title: New harness supply dependency has not reached the DFA
findings.anchor: *Not yet applied:* VIN as a common cause
findings.analysis: The current hardware review explicitly leaves the shared VIN dependency unapplied in WP-A-03. Drawing-derived box power-loss effects are hypotheses pending physical confirmation; the independence argument must account for this dependency before accepting stock PCS availability.
findings.author_action: Crosswalk HB-03 and F-02 to DFI-01/06 and IC-05; identify power domains, supply-loss causes, affected safety mechanisms and recovery. Propose DFA and affected fault-tree/FFI/test changes without assigning diagnostic credit.
findings.closure_evidence: Reviewed configuration-bound power topology and DFA, actual VS-HW-22 evidence, and human disposition of IC-05 and DQ-209.

findings.title: Hardware summary metrics predate the revised FMEDA
findings.analysis: WP-H-03 still reports the former generic SG-07 values. The newer hardware review reports SG-009 (mapped to SG-07) SPFM changing to 85.9%, and fmeda-sg009.yaml is revision 0.3. The summary and calculation baseline need reconciliation; neither set is demonstrated hardware compliance.
findings.author_action: Recompute from the pinned YAML with its documented algorithm; record the SG-009/SG-07 identity mapping, input revision and generic-rate limitations. Reconcile every summary and sensitivity table, including totals/LFM/PMHF; do not copy only the SPFM number.
findings.closure_evidence: Reproducible calculation, independently checked source-to-summary reconciliation and revised WP-H-03; BOM-based metrics remain separately open.

findings.title: Heartbeat siren criteria use unresolved clock origins
findings.analysis: VS-FI-10 states siren <=0.5 s but records approximately 0.56 s after the last heartbeat. Section 4 instead says <=0.5 s after detection. VS-FI-09 also uses 0.5 s without an explicit clock. These are not interchangeable; the record cannot establish failure or success until the clock and tolerance are explicit.
findings.author_action: Provide a timing-event dictionary (fault onset, last valid heartbeat, detection, revocation, physical acoustic onset). Map each criterion to its governing requirement and clock, budget task phase/jitter and instrument uncertainty, and propose consistent VS-FI/VS-UV/VS-VAL wording.
findings.closure_evidence: Reviewed event definitions and requirement trace, actual synchronized target/acoustic measurements, worst-case margin and anomaly disposition. Do not reset the clock to remove a discrepancy.

findings.title: Fault injection coverage excludes the later SFMEA rows
findings.analysis: The plan itself says SFMEA-33 through SFMEA-40 still need cases (OI-6). A structurally valid trace map or the existing 31 case IDs does not establish coverage of these eight analysis rows.
findings.proposed_owner_role: Safety analysis owner / fault injection lead
findings.author_action: For each of SFMEA-33 through SFMEA-40, map cause, mechanism, observable safe state, requirement, injection level and exact case ID. Show justified non-injectable analyses separately; preserve shared-case dependencies and known gaps.
findings.closure_evidence: Reviewed complete per-row crosswalk, controlled test specifications, actual execution records or justified alternative analyses, and independent review. Case authoring alone is not closure.

findings.title: Two review records share the same review identifier
findings.analysis: The management audit pre-review and the hardware source review both use RR-2026-010. Their paths distinguish them, but bare-ID citations cannot. This ambiguity was introduced by the audit publication alongside the concurrent hardware review; neither record supplies independent verification credit.
findings.author_action: Agree an identifier namespace or reserve a unique replacement ID after checking all review folders. Produce a controlled migration/citation crosswalk; retain historical records and sealed audit hashes. Use full paths immediately in all new references.
findings.closure_evidence: Human-approved identification rule, collision-free index and verified current links with preserved historical provenance. No record silently overwritten.

findings.title: Validation result template omits three specified cases
findings.analysis: The external-measure cases VS-VAL-30, VS-VAL-31 and VS-VAL-32 are specified but absent from the section 7.2 result template. The template may be expanded during execution; this is a documentary completeness observation, not proof that testing was missed. Twelve ML cases also have no case-level result table in WP-W-10, whose current-status narrative must be considered separately.
findings.author_action: Add controlled result-template rows or an explicit cross-reference to the result record for each external-measure case. Include configuration, observed values, criterion, anomaly and evidence links. Keep all outcomes unexecuted until actual evidence is recorded.
findings.closure_evidence: Reviewed specification-to-report crosswalk covering VS-VAL-30 through VS-VAL-32, with correct unexecuted state until execution. No inference of test success from a filled template.
